sources.title: The House
sources.summary: Rusticated Braggville pink granite faces a brick structure above Illinois dolomite. E-shaped plan fronts east/north/west lot edges; south courtyard admits light. Over 17,000 square feet; service space exceeds half. Three family, two guest, eight servant bedrooms; eleven fireplaces; seven staircases. Post-family institutional use began after 1936; 1946 conversion, 1966 preservation purchase.
sources.evidence_limit: Granite thickness stated 8–10 inches here conflicts with about seven inches in G03; modern description is not a dated 1904 inventory.

sources.title: The Collection — architectural and household evidence
sources.summary: Richardson sketch dated May 14, 1885. John Glessner’s 1923 memoir includes 25 typed pages, floorplans and Kaufmann & Fabry photographs, including two unique Fanny-bedroom views. Kitchen annunciator used twelve call buttons. A 1965 sale flyer records institutional plans and paved courtyard; museum corrects its stone-veneer claim to about seven inches.
sources.evidence_limit: Collection essays span many years. Date every object; 1923 photographs and 1965 plans are not direct 1904 snapshots. Original memoir not fully acquired.

sources.title: Exterior from Inland Architect

dates.publication_detail: The Inland Architect and News Record, vol. XI no. 1

sources.summary: Period exterior photograph and first-floor sketch published two months after the family moved in.
sources.evidence_limit: Provides 1888 baseline, not automatic proof of unchanged 1904 details.

sources.title: Porte Cochere doors
sources.summary: Period front driveway doors; these sheltered carriage arrivals. Museum used the photograph to recreate doors removed during the 1950s for an overhead garage door.
sources.evidence_limit: Historic photo is direct baseline; present restored doors should be cross-checked against it.

sources.title: Double Bough
sources.summary: Corner guest-room Morris & Co. wallpaper selected after electrification in 1892, selected again in 1916; current paper is a 2015 reproduction.
sources.evidence_limit: Supports 1904 pattern attribution, not proof of exact surviving shade or condition.

sources.title: Electricity comes to Glessner House
sources.source_type: official museum blog citing family correspondence
sources.summary: July 1892 correspondence documents electric conversion, repainting and a gas explosion. Original gas fixtures in main hall/parlor were converted. Parlor received Pretyman wall covering; other rooms Morris papers. Kerosene lamps remained in use in 1901. Basement wood conduit survives. 1923 photos show some changed fixtures of unknown installation date.
sources.evidence_limit: Do not infer 1904 fixtures from all 1923 photographs. Original prewiring is presumed in article, not confirmed by building specifications.

sources.title: Glessner Family
sources.summary: Frances established a basement workbench in 1904 for silverwork.
sources.evidence_limit: Exact installation month, equipment inventory and room dimensions require journal verification.

sources.title: Heating Glessner House — Then and Now
sources.summary: Source discusses original heating and quotes the 1923 memoir. A photographed thermostat was made by a company organized in 1904.
sources.evidence_limit: Company founding gives only a terminus post quem, not proof that this thermostat existed in the 1904 house.

sources.title: Preservation Month Part I — Dining Room
sources.summary: Dining-room gas fixtures converted in 1892 with glass shades added. Iznik fireplace tiles removed by Frances Glessner Lee in 1938; later recreated.
sources.evidence_limit: Track originals versus recreated surfaces; historic photos are required for 1904 placement.

sources.title: Preservation Month Part II — Main Hall
sources.summary: Includes George Glessner’s earliest known main-hall photograph and discussion of later restoration.
sources.evidence_limit: Modern restoration is an interpretive reconstruction; date historic views separately.

sources.title: Stone capitals on Glessner House
sources.summary: Examines capital design; Isaac Scott proposals were not accepted by the Glessners.
sources.evidence_limit: Rejected designs must not be modeled as executed ornament.

sources.title: A Tale of Thirty-Five Tiles
sources.summary: Documents master-bedroom tile restoration and return from family ownership.
sources.evidence_limit: Use to distinguish removed/reinstalled originals from twentieth-century conditions.

sources.title: Datestone
sources.summary: North-facing east-end gable bears A.D. and 1886 datestones; journal places near-completion of exterior stonework in November 1886.
sources.evidence_limit: 1886 date stone is not occupancy year; finished house occupied in December 1887.

sources.title: Research Opportunities
sources.summary: Museum holds historic photographs, family papers, restoration files, drawings and published articles. Appointment-based access.
sources.evidence_limit: Collections are not comprehensively digitized. No appointment or contact was made.

sources.evidence_limit: Exact Glessner series/item numbers and drawings still require extraction. Direct open rate-limited; indexed record verified.

Do not invent footprint, heights, floor elevations, roof pitches or openings from uninspected drawing thumbnails.
1911 Sanborn maps are later evidence; backcast only after change review.
